messages:
zoe: Customer POC (Zenith) reports SSE streams in Safari drop with partial JSON then parser error. Chrome fine. They attached security questionnaire and asked for Dedicated pricing 99— blocking sign-off.

mike: ask them to run a raw curl: `curl -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \"https://poc.redwood.ai/zenith/stream\" -v` and paste output.

zoe: they ran curl; connection stays open but no bytes for ~18-22s, then partial data. Browser shows `EventSource failed to parse event`.

anjali: likely intermediate buffering or keepalive mismatch. Our heartbeat is 15s; some CDNs coalesce chunks. Quick mitigation: set heartbeat=6s, send comment pings every 4s, and add `Cache-Control: no-transform` + `X-Accel-Buffering: no`.

mike: deploying a canary patch to the POC route with those headers now. Also infra-bot shows a few 429s from their debug IP 9203.0.113.77; I'll whitelist for 2h to avoid rate-limit closures.

ops-bot: route_patch applied route=poc/zenith canary_id=cp-1932 heartbeat=6s headers=[Cache-Control:no-transform,X-Accel-Buffering:no] ts=2026-03-22T11:04:12Z

zoe: customer also on SDK v0.9.0 per screenshot. There was a known bug for split UTF-8 across chunks fixed in v0.9.2+. Ask them to upgrade; if they can't, recommend `event-source-polyfill` or enable websocket fallback.

mike: enabled ws fallback on their route as a temporary workaround. ops-bot: ws_fallback=enabled for poc/zenith.

zoe: customer retried Safari with ws fallback and reports stable stream. They've asked for a short Dedicated POC price and SOC2 attestation text.

sales-bot: Draft: "Dedicated POC: 1 GPU reserved lane, estimated $9k9k/month (US-West) depending on region; includes VPC peering, KMS integration, and audit logs. SOC2 Type II attestation available; full questionnaire responses attached on request."

zoe: sending pricing + SOC2 note to customer now and asking them to upgrade SDK. Follow-ups: revert canary and ws-fallback after SDK upgrade confirmed. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
